paragraphs.title: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion
paragraphs.hi: एकसमान त्वरण से गतिमान वस्तु का

en.q: If the velocity of a particle is v = At + Bt<sup>2</sup>, where A and B are constants, then the distance travelled by it between 1 s and 2 s is :

en.q: Two cars P and Q start from a point at the same time in a straight line and their positions are represented by X<sub>P</sub>(t) = at + bt<sup>2</sup> and X<sub>Q</sub>(t) = ft − t<sup>2</sup>. At what time do the cars have the same velocity?

en.q: Preeti reached the metro station and found that the escalator was not working. She walked up the stationary escalator in time t<sub>1</sub>. On other days, if she remains stationary on the moving escalator, then the escalator takes her up in time t<sub>2</sub>. The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be :

en.q: A toy car with charge q moves on a frictionless horizontal plane surface under the influence of a uniform electric field E⃗. Due to the force qE⃗, its velocity increases from 0 to 6 m/s in one second duration. At that instant the direction of the field is reversed. The car continues to move for two more seconds under the influence of this field. The average velocity and the average speed of the toy car between 0 to 3 seconds are respectively :

en.q: A ball is thrown vertically downward with a velocity of 20 m/s from the top of a tower. It hits the ground after some time with a velocity of 80 m/s. The height of the tower is : (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)

en.q: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t = 0. Let S<sub>n</sub> be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t = n − 1 to t = n. Then, the ratio S<sub>n</sub>/S<sub>n+1</sub> is :

en.q: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity 4 m s<sup>−1</sup>. The ball strikes the water surface after 4 s. The height of bridge above water surface is : (Take g = 10 m s<sup>−2</sup>)

en.q: The velocity v–time t plot of the motion of a body is shown below. The acceleration a–time t graph that best suits this motion is :
o: [graph A: a rises, stays flat, falls back to zero (same shape as v)]
[graph B: a rises then stays constant]
[graph C: positive constant, zero, then negative constant]
[graph D: negative constant, then rising line]

review.keyCheck: Answer printed in the copy: 3; matches our solving
review.keySource: eSaral copy's printed key (neet-sources/neet-papers/2024/physics-with-solutions.pdf; right edge clipped, read from page images; clipped option ends completed from the copy's solutions or list logic). No NTA final key for 2024 in neet-sources yet.
review.note: v–t: zero, linear rise, constant, linear fall to zero. Options are graphs; needs redrawn figures.

en.q: Two cities X and Y are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every T min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction X to Y notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period T of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.

review.keySource: NTA final answer key, NEET (UG) 2025, Code 45 (neet-sources/neet-papers/2025/nta-final-answer-key-code-45.pdf); text from the Aakash Code 45 answers-and-solutions scan (neet-sources/neet-papers/2025/full-paper-with-solutions.pdf; read from page images)

en.q:
When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. (g = 9.8 m s−2)
A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s.
B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s.
C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s.
D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s.
E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s.
What is the correct order of the distance travelled by the ruler for each person?

review.keySource: Answer key Codes 11–14 (neet-sources/neet-papers/2026/answer-key-codes-11-14.pdf), Code 13 (content/keys/neet-official-keys.json); text from the Code 13 question booklet scan (neet-sources/neet-papers/2026/question-booklet-code-13-with-answers.pdf; read from page images)

en.q:
The following plots show variation of velocity (v) with time (t), of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct?
A. v falls linearly to zero, then rises linearly (V shape above the axis)
B. v rises linearly, then falls linearly to zero (Λ shape)
C. straight line falling from a positive value through zero to negative values
D. straight line rising from a negative value through zero to positive values
E. U-shaped curve above the axis

review.keySource: Answer key Codes 11–14 (neet-sources/neet-papers/2026/answer-key-codes-11-14.pdf), Code 13 (content/keys/neet-official-keys.json); text from the Code 13 question booklet scan (neet-sources/neet-papers/2026/question-booklet-code-13-with-answers.pdf; read from page images)
review.note: The five v–t plots are described in the stem; redrawn figures would help.
